statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of seven representative public states. Authenticated account changes, financial applications and real agent-contact submission were excluded to avoid credentials or external side effects.

page.notes: Large UK property marketplace. Five principal archetypes plus login and not-found behavior were sampled. Geographic/property permutations sharing these templates were not exhaustively tested.

paths.description: Entry page and property-search start; represents global header, search and consent experience.
Representative South London property-results template and list browsing journey.
Representative property-detail template and route to agent contact.
Primary valuation form surface, including empty postcode validation probe.
Authentication entry inspected for autocomplete and passkey/WebAuthn support.
Unknown route inspected for HTTP status and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the body remained rgb(255,255,255), text remained rgb(83,83,95), and computed color-scheme was normal. The dark screenshot is visually identical to the light capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint page and consent surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Persistent chrome does not react to scroll state
findings.evidence: The listing scroll video shows the same full filter/header chrome while content moves; no progress or reduced chrome state appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact scrolled state or a meaningful progress/position cue without obscuring results.

findings.summary: Cookie consent blocks the entire first view
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots on every representative route show a modal covering the primary content before interaction. On mobile it occupies most of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the first-load interruption, keep equally prominent reject controls, and preserve access to core content where lawful.

findings.summary: The modal is not implemented with the native dialog primitive
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found aria-modal=1 but zero <dialog> elements and zero popovers on home, listing, detail and valuation routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with showModal(), labelled structure, platform focus handling and an explicit dismiss path.

findings.summary: Several controls have undersized pointer targets
findings.evidence: The DOM probes found at least 30 visible controls below 24px in one dimension; the listing clear button also lacks an accessible name. Focus itself was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, preferably 44 by 44 for primary touch controls, without reducing visible focus.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a misleading success response
findings.evidence: A deliberately unknown URL returned HTTP 200 rather than 404. The captured first view remained behind the consent interstitial, weakening error recognition and recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the correct 404 status and render a clear not-found state with search, home and back recovery actions.

findings.summary: The listing template is far outside good load thresholds
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured listing LCP at 33,720ms, TBT at 1,121.5ms and performance 0.38. Home LCP was 2,646.6ms and TBT 634.5ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the listing LCP chain, prioritize its hero/result content, and remove main-thread work until LCP and interaction latency are in the good range.

findings.summary: Heavy script work blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1,121.5ms TBT on listing and 634.5ms on home; the trace also recorded a 92.87ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Split long tasks, defer nonessential tags and advertising, and schedule noncritical work after the primary content becomes interactive.

findings.summary: The initial network is dominated by script and third parties
findings.evidence: The home HAR recorded 65 requests and 2.93MB transferred, including 1.99MB script and 2.46MB third-party bytes. It also found a parser-inserted stylesheet and script candidates plus an uncompressed JS resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical chains, defer nonessential scripts and tags, compress all text resources, and apply useful caching.

findings.summary: The listing ships large amounts of unused and duplicated code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,514,686 bytes of unused JavaScript and 46,116 bytes of unused CSS; a featured-customer bundle appears repeatedly in the waste list.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, remove duplicate injections, and load advertising/experimentation code only when needed and consented.

findings.summary: Listing controls have broken names, roles and labels
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unnamed clear button, an unlabeled sort select, prohibited aria-label on a roleless div, and repeated visible Contact labels that do not match their accessible names.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control one accurate accessible name, associate visible labels with inputs, add valid roles before ARIA, and keep visible and accessible labels aligned.

findings.summary: Heading structure skips levels on key templates
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order on listing; its footer jumps to H4. DOM probes also show H1 followed directly by H3 on listing and article routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings to express a sequential document outline while retaining the currently visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow works, but target sizing remains inadequate
findings.evidence: All five mobile layouts had zero horizontal overflow and viewport scaling was allowed, but probes repeatedly found at least 30 visible controls smaller than 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the successful reflow and enlarge hit areas; verify at 200% and 400% zoom with keyboard and touch.

findings.summary: A monitoring endpoint fails during normal load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the HAR recorded repeated HTTP 401 failures from the Elastic APM RUM intake endpoint.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or suppress the invalid monitoring request so normal page loads produce no console/network errors.

findings.summary: Images are unsized, oversized or distorted
findings.evidence: The image probe found all four home images missing width/height, all four oversized and three legacy JPEGs; Lighthouse found multiple estate-agent logos rendered at aspect ratios that do not match source assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic dimensions, generate correctly cropped logo variants, serve modern responsive formats and right-size each source.

findings.summary: Production bundles expose broken or absent source-map links
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found many large first-party scripts with missing maps and several advertised .map URLs returning 400/404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid restricted source maps or remove invalid sourceMappingURL references, and monitor DevTools inspector issues.

findings.summary: Canonical and status signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Home and valuation probes found no canonical URL, while an unknown route returned HTTP 200. The site does provide robots.txt, a large sitemap and canonical URLs on listing/detail/article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonicals where appropriate and return correct 404 statuses while preserving current sitemap and robots signals.

findings.summary: Commercial entity pages lack structured data
findings.evidence: The property detail and listing probes found zero JSON-LD blocks; home also lacked Organization/WebSite JSON-LD. The article template was the only sampled route with JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org WebSite/Organization, ItemList and real-estate entity markup plus complete Open Graph metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Core transport and content defenses are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but found no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options. The cookies primitive reported all eight observed cookies without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS and nosniff, deploy a restrictive nonce/hash CSP, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with appropriate SameSite and HttpOnly attributes.

findings.summary: Tracking starts with a very large third-party footprint
findings.evidence: Before consent choice, the HAR recorded 49 third-party requests and 2.46MB third-party transfer. The tracker probe found 11 third-party origins and five known tracker domains; the dialog names 215 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to the minimum necessary vendors and events, prevent nonessential tag downloads before consent, and batch the remaining analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication lacks modern autofill and passkey signals
findings.evidence: The login probe found an email input with no autocomplete token and no passkey/WebAuthn text or code signal. No permission prompt appeared on sampled page loads.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=username/email, offer passkey registration and conditional authentication, and continue requesting permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are missing
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP and HSTS. Several first-party cookies use SameSite=None without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; remove unnecessary SameSite=None cookies and evaluate Trusted Types.

findings.summary: HTTP failure semantics are not resilient
findings.evidence: The unknown-route test returned 200 OK rather than a 404 status, so caches, crawlers and users cannot reliably distinguish failure from success.
findings.suggestedFix: Return accurate HTTP statuses and a server-rendered recovery page that remains useful without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Language and directional foundations are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Sampled pages use en, en-GB and en-US despite UK content. Inline-CSS probing found logical-property use on home but not on listing, detail, article or valuation templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Standardize accurate lang values per locale, declare direction where needed and migrate reusable layout spacing to logical properties.

findings.summary: The valuation postcode field has no enforceable empty-state feedback
findings.evidence: The valuation probe found postcodeInput is not required; its empty value reports checkValidity() true, aria-invalid is absent, and no alert/error text was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the requirement programmatic, validate after interaction, focus the field on submission failure and announce a specific error through a live region.

findings.summary: Key inputs opt out of useful browser assistance
findings.evidence: The login email field has an empty autocomplete value, the valuation postcode has none, and location search explicitly uses autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply accurate autocomplete tokens such as email/username and postal-code; do not disable browser autofill where it helps users.

findings.summary: The sign-in entry does not advertise phishing-resistant authentication
findings.evidence: The login surface offers email continuation only; the probe found no WebAuthn/passkey signal and the email input lacks autocomplete. Actual account changes were excluded to avoid side effects.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys alongside recovery-safe email sign-in and make account/cancellation commitments explicit before any irreversible action.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes image bytes
findings.evidence: All four probed home images were oversized for their rendered size, four lacked intrinsic dimensions and three used JPEG; below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate modern responsive variants, preserve dimensions and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Large unused scripts and failed telemetry consume resources
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1.51MB unused JS on listing, while home loads repeated analytics/advertising tags and sends APM requests that fail with 401.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate/vendor work, conditionally import optional features, defer background processing and stop failed telemetry retries.

findings.summary: Third-party code is disproportionate to first-view value
findings.evidence: On home, 49 of 65 requests and 2.46 of 2.93MB transferred were third-party; Google Tag Manager alone accounted for about 1.25MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, load vendors after consent and user need, and remove redundant tag containers.

findings.summary: Property capabilities are not exposed in a structured agent-facing form
findings.evidence: The sampled routes expose no WebMCP/agent tool signals, property pages lack JSON-LD, robots.txt blocks GPTBot, and Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.33 on listing.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent access is an intended channel, expose narrowly scoped search/save/contact tools with confirmation and machine-readable property metadata.
